angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 141,923 km at 55.60 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 17.9847 +/- 0.0412 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 55.60 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.204 +/- 0.004 solar radii from Hori et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-2406 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..289H/abstract): 141,923 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.166 +/- 0.004 solar masses from Hori et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-2406 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..289H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3100 +/- 31 K from Hori et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2406 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..289H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hori et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-2406 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024AJ....167..289H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-2406.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.039, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
